"'''Ozymandias'''"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blog.zap2it.com/frominsidethebox/2013/07/breaking-bad-new-pics-episode-titles-and-everything-else-we-know-about-season-5b.html|title='Breaking Bad': New pics, episode titles and everything else we know about Season 5b|work=Zap2It|last=Porter|first=Rick|date=July 16, 2013|accessdate=July 17, 2013}}</ref> is the fourteenth episode of the [[Breaking Bad (season 5)|fifth season]] of the American television drama series ''[[Breaking Bad]]'', and the 60th overall episode of the series. Written by [[Moira Walley-Beckett]] and directed by [[Rian Johnson]], it aired on [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] in the United States and Canada on September 15, 2013.

==Plot==
A flashback to when [[Walter White (Breaking Bad)|Walter White]] and [[Jesse Pinkman]] [[Pilot (Breaking Bad)|first cooked]] [[methamphetamine]] in [[Tohajiilee Indian Reservation|To'hajiilee]] shows Walt calling a pregnant [[Skyler White|Skyler]] and making up an excuse for why he will be late. Skyler suggests the name [[Holly (name)|Holly]] for their baby, which Walt finds agreeable.

In present at To'hajiilee, in the aftermath of the shootout, [[Hank Schrader|Hank]] is wounded with a bullet in his leg, [[Steven Gomez|Gomez]] has been killed and Jack's gang is left unscathed. Jack orders some men to search for Jesse and prepares to kill Hank after cornering him. Walt grovels to Jack to spare his brother-in-law, offering Jack his entire $80 million fortune buried near them and asking Hank to swear that he will not pursue what has just happened for his own safety. Hank refuses to beg for his life and confirms he is DEA, marveling that the brilliant Walter can't see that Jack made up his mind ten minutes ago. Hank tells Jack to go ahead, and Jack shoots him in the head before he can even finish his last words; Walt collapses to the ground in total despair.

Jack's team uses Walt's coordinates to locate and unearth the seven buried barrels of money, loading six into their trucks but leaving one for Walt. Walt spots Jesse's hiding place and betrays him to the men, reminding Jack that the hit on Jesse was never carried out. Jesse is dragged out screaming and is almost killed, but Todd suggests they first interrogate him to find out what information he supplied to the DEA. Walt reveals to Jesse his presence during [[List of Breaking Bad characters#Jane_Margolis|Jane]]'s death before Jack's gang takes Jesse away. At Todd's headquarters, a beaten and scared Jesse is detained in a cell. Todd escorts him in chains to a meth lab, where he is tethered. Jesse notices a photograph of Andrea and Brock as Todd instructs him to begin cooking.

Due to a bullet having hit his fuel tank, Walt quickly runs out of gas while driving home. Abandoning his car, Walt rolls the money barrel through the desert until arriving at a house and buying the owner's truck. Meanwhile, at the car wash, Marie informs Skyler that Walt was arrested by Hank and is in custody. With Walt now apparently caught, Marie offers to support her sister and their family and asks for the false confessions implicating Hank to be destroyed and Walter Jr. be told the truth. Walter Jr. is left in disbelief at the entire story when told by Skyler and Marie.

When Skyler and Walter Jr. return home, they discover Walt hurriedly packing while ordering them to do the same. In a rush, Walt promises to explain everything later, but Skyler assumes he has killed Hank when he cannot answer to his whereabouts. Skyler grabs a kitchen knife and orders Walt to leave their home, but when he refuses, she lunges at him and cuts his hand. In the ensuing fight, Walter Jr. pulls Walt off Skyler and calls the police, claiming that Walt attacked her with a knife and has already killed Hank. Walt takes Holly and leaves in the truck, while a distressed Skyler runs after him. Alone with his daughter, Walt is moved when Holly's only utterances are for her mother.

The police soon arrive, as does Marie. They tap into the Whites' home phone and try tracing it when Walt eventually calls. After Skyler tells him that she is alone, Walt berates her, accusing her of never supporting his criminal activities and having himself worked alone in building up the wealth for their family. Suppressing his intense weeping, he ruthlessly claims responsibility for killing Hank, to Marie's horror, while threatening the same to Skyler should she divulge his doings to anyone else. When Skyler apologizes and simply wishes for Holly to be returned, Walt tells her he still has things left to do, then destroys his phone and leaves Holly in at a nearby fire station with their home address written on a note. The next morning he is picked up by Saul's contact in order to leave Albuquerque and be given a new identity somewhere else.

==Production==
{{unreferenced section|date=September 2013}}
The episode was written by Moira Walley-Beckett and directed by Rian Johnson. It aired on AMC in the United States and Canada on September 15, 2013.

==Music==
The song used in the episode is "Take My True Love by the Hand" by [[The Limeliters]].

==Title reference==
The title of this episode is a reference to [[Ozymandias]], the [[Percy Bysshe Shelley]] poem of the same name that recounts the crumbling legacy of a once proud king. At the end of the fifth episode of ''[[Talking Bad]]'', [[Vince Gilligan]] emphasized the line "Look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!" in reference to Walt and his fallen empire.

In a 2013 trailer for the series, [[Bryan Cranston]] recites the entire poem.<ref name="hufff">{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/07/30/breaking-bad-ozymandias-teaser_n_3676122.html|title='Breaking Bad' 'Ozymandias' Teaser Sounds Ominous|last=Moaba|first=Alex|date=July 30, 2013|work=[[The Huffington Post]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref><ref name="bbc">{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/blogs-magazine-monitor-23528902|title=Why did Breaking Bad use Ozymandias?|date=August 1, 2013|work=[[BBC News Magazine Monitor]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Viewers===
The episode was watched by 6.4 million viewers on its original broadcast, becoming the most watched episode of the show's history.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bibel |first=Sara |title= Breaking Bad' Delivers a Record 6.4 Million Viewers |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2013/09/16/breaking-bad-delivers-a-record-6-4-million-viewers/203074/|work=TV by the Numbers|date=September 16, 2013|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref>

===Reception===
The episode received widespread critical acclaim and was described by several publications as the series' best episode.<ref name="meta">{{cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/feature/breaking-bad-episode-514-ozymandias-reviews|title=Episode Review: Breaking Bad, "Ozymandias"|last=Dietz|first=Jason|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[Metacritic]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref> Critics praised the acting by the cast, directing by Rian Johnson and writing by Moira Walley-Beckett.<ref name="hit">{{cite web|url=http://www.hitfix.com/whats-alan-watching/review-breaking-bad-ozymandias-roll-out-the-barrel|title=Review: 'Breaking Bad' - 'Ozymandias': Roll out the barrel|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[HitFix]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref><ref name="av">{{cite web|url=http://www.avclub.com/articles/ozymandias,102436/|title=Breaking Bad: Ozymandias|last=Bowman|first=Donna|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[The A.V. Club]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref><ref name="huff">{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/maureen-ryan/breaking-bad-ozymandias_b_3931402.html|title='Breaking Bad' 'Ozymandias' Recap: Devastation|last=Ryan|first=Maureen|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[The Huffington Post]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref> Seth Amitin of [[IGN]] called the episode the "most gut-wrenching, twisted, horrific, and well-planned" episode of the series thus far and described it as "a capitalization on all of the built-up pieces that add up to a puzzle." Amitin additionally lauded the episode's directing and acting, stating that he could "taste" the episode's "cruelty and bitter tears".<ref name="IGN">{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2013/09/16/breaking-bad-ozymandias-review|title=NO CALM. ALL STORM.|last=Amitin|first=Seth|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[IGN]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref> James Poniewozik of [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine]] noted the significance of both phone conversations between Walt and Skyler, marking the beginning and the end of his journey, respectively.<ref name="time">{{cite web|url=http://entertainment.time.com/2013/09/16/breaking-bad-watch-take-good-care-of-my-baby/|title=''Breaking Bad'' Watch: Take Good Care of My Baby|last=Poniewozik|first=James|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[Time magazine]]|accessdate=September 16, 2013}}</ref> Maureen Ryan of ''[[Huffington Post]]'' stated that the episode was indescribable and "the hardest episode of TV I ever watched", describing it as "mind-bendingly, soul-churningly devastating" and sickening.<ref name="huff" /> Tim Surette of [[TV.com]] compared the sight of Walt rolling the money barrel in the desert to a [[dung beetle]].<ref name="TV">{{cite web|url=http://www.tv.com/shows/breaking-bad/community/post/breaking-bad-season-5-episode-14-ozymandias-review-137900307447/|title=''Breaking Bad'' "Ozymandias" Review: Family Feud|last=Surette|first=Tim|date=September 15, 2013|work=[[TV.com]]|accessdate=September 17, 2013}}</ref> Tom Mendelson of ''[[The Independent]]'' speculated that the episode may be the best television episode ever written.<ref>http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/features/is-breaking-bads-ozymandias-the-greatest-episode-of-tv-ever-written-8821985.html</ref>
On the Breaking Bad Insider podcast, Vince Gilligan revealed that he considers the episode to be the best of the series.<ref name="podcast">{{cite AV media|people=Dixon, Kelly and Gilligan, Vince|year=2013|title=Breaking Bad Insider Podcast|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/podcast/breaking-bad-insider-514/id311058181|format=[[podcast]]|publisher=[[iTunes]]|accessdate=September 17, 2013}}</ref>
